# Sales Tax Pricing Index

> A sourced comparison of pricing for every major sales tax compliance platform serving US ecommerce and SaaS businesses. Eight providers tracked: Anrok, Avalara, Kintsugi, Numeral, Sphere, TaxCloud, TaxJar, and Zamp.

## Publisher

The Sales Tax Pricing Index is operated by TaxCloud, Inc. (taxcloud.com), one of the eight providers compared. Ownership is disclosed at the bottom of every page and at /methodology#ownership. Despite the publisher relationship, the site is built and maintained as a sourced public reference. Every price is sourced from public vendor pricing pages, vendor help-center articles, public buyer-review platforms (G2, TrustRadius, Shopify App Store), or third-party aggregators (Vendr, checkthat.ai). No price is invented. Quote-only vendors are surfaced as ranges from public buyer reports, not point estimates.

## Editorial methodology

- Every dollar figure traces to a public, dated source. Confidence ratings (A–G: A = vendor pricing page, B = help center/docs, C = third-party aggregator, D = blog/PR, E = public forum, F = internal/customer-shared, G = estimated with disclosed methodology) are attached to each price point.
- Opaque vendors (Avalara, Zamp) are shown as ranges from aggregator buyer data, not point estimates. "Quote required" stays "quote required."
- The calculator runs the same pricing math used to populate per-provider pages, with no separate logic.
- TaxCloud's pricing is sourced first-party (we publish full plan, order-tier, and filings-tier ladders); other providers are sourced from their own public materials wherever possible.
- Buyer-observation sections cite only public, non-TaxCloud sources. TaxCloud's internal sales-call data is not used as a source for public claims.

## Category pages (no vendor named in the query)

- What sales tax software costs: https://salestaxpricingindex.org/how-much-does-sales-tax-software-cost (annual cost bands for two published buyer profiles, the four pricing models in the category, entry prices, and the cost items no vendor publishes)
- Cheapest sales tax software: https://salestaxpricingindex.org/cheapest-sales-tax-software (ranked on published pricing across several buyer profiles, with the profiles where the answer changes shown alongside the ones where it does not, plus capability gates that make price the wrong question; on a profile with a hard requirement, platforms that cannot meet it are removed from the ranking rather than allowed to win on cost)
- Hidden fees: https://salestaxpricingindex.org/sales-tax-software-hidden-fees (every fee category across all tracked platforms, each cell marked published / unpublished / not charged / unknown, plus a four-point fee disclosure score per vendor)
- Cost to switch: https://salestaxpricingindex.org/cost-to-switch-from-{provider} for each of the eight slugs (run-rate difference, published exit terms, one-time onboarding cost, payback period, and an explicit list of switching costs the site refuses to estimate)

## Key structural claims

- Of the eight providers tracked, TaxCloud and Avalara are the only Streamlined Sales Tax (SST) Certified Service Providers. CSP status is a regulatory designation by the SST Governing Board; vendors cannot self-claim it. CSP-certified vendors provide free filing services in the 24 SST member states for sellers with economic-nexus-only presence (no physical nexus).
- The other six providers (TaxJar, Numeral, Kintsugi, Anrok, Sphere, Zamp) are not SST CSPs and bill standard per-filing rates in SST states.
- Pricing models on the site fall into four buckets, by each provider's primary model: tiered subscription on order volume (TaxCloud, TaxJar), per filing and per registration (Kintsugi, Numeral), flat rate per state or region (Anrok, Sphere), and quote-only (Avalara, Zamp). No tracked provider prices on a straight percentage of revenue. Avalara is in the quote-only bucket because its enterprise motion defines it and its ERP and $50M-plus segments remain quote-only; it does also publish a per-state list rate for sub-$50M buyers on a fixed list of non-ERP integrations, which the calculator uses for those buyers.
- "Cheapest" on this site always means cheapest on published pricing for a stated buyer profile. Two of the eight platforms are quote-only, so their ranked position is an observed range from buyer data rather than a price, and a negotiated contract can land below it. The site does not claim to know what any vendor's negotiated pricing is.
- "Hidden fee" on this site has one narrow meaning: a charge that exists and that the vendor does not put a number on. It does not mean expensive and it is not used as an accusation. TaxCloud, the site's publisher, appears in several of those rows, including as the only tracked vendor with a published credit card surcharge.
- Switching sales tax platforms does not normally require re-registering with the states. Sales tax permits are issued to the business, not to the software vendor, so per-state registration fees are a cost of expanding rather than a cost of switching. Sellers enrolled in the Streamlined Sales Tax program do have to reassign their Certified Service Provider selection.
- The site publishes no estimate for the internal-hours cost of implementing or switching platforms, the cost of a parallel run, or historical data migration. These are real and often larger than the run-rate difference, and any figure would be invented.

## What this site is and isn't

Is: a sourced comparison surface with public price citations, a free calculator, and per-provider transparency ratings.

Isn't: a paid review site, an affiliate-driven directory, or a TaxCloud marketing landing page. There are no affiliate links, no embedded vendor CTAs, and no demo-booking forms.

## Date

Content is refreshed on a rolling basis. Every page displays a "Last updated" timestamp. The most recent provider-level verifications are tracked in /changelog.
